subject: Compute handshake: capacity, isolation, and SLA alignment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@medora.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compute handshake: capacity, isolation, and SLA alignment

Hi Sofia — thanks for the call this morning. Quick write-up so we all have the same view and a clear set of next actions. Please correct anything I miss.

Summary of the customer's goals and pain points
- Goal: Move inference for Medora's clinical-annotation pipeline to a dedicated, SLA-backed offering to meet 95th pct latency targets and PHI isolation requirements.
- Pain: Current self-hosted setup is brittle under bursts, KV cache cold starts add ~40-60ms per request, and ops team lacks single-pane instrumentation across model versions.
- Scale: Expected steady-state 150 qps (avg payloads ~512 tokens), peak ~400 qps during batch uploads.
- Isolation: Need tenant isolation at the pool level (no multi-tenant GPUs for PHI), plus audit logs for model access.

Technical outline we discussed
- Reserved pool: 6x A100-equivalent slots initially; 2x burstable slots for short peaks.
- KV/prefix caching: plan to warm cold paths for highest-volume patient flows.
- Quantization: test 8-bit for non-critical models; keep critical scoring models at fp16.
- Observability: token-level latency breakdown, tenant-level tracing, and an exportable audit trail.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability for the pool; latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for interactive endpoints.

Commercial asks from Medora that we captured
- Desired contract: 12-month reserved capacity with monthly usage true-ups.
- Procurement timeline: procurement kicks off mid-June; engineering embargo/airgap review within 3 weeks.

Next steps (owners & timing)
- Karthik: Share a compact Ops/Procurement pack (attached) and preliminary SLA draft by EOD today.
- Jonas: Prepare the internal pricing carve to support a dedicated 12-month commit (by Wed).
- Vanessa: Coordinate security addendum template and confirm KMS options with the security team (by next Tue).
- Sofia / Medora: Confirm whether SOC2 evidence request can be scoped to monthly snapshots vs full audit (answer requested by Jun 14).

Attachments: preliminary SLA draft (SLA-draft-Redwood-Medora-20270607.pdf), capacity matrix (capacity-proposal-ops-matrix.xlsx).

Thank you again — I've marked the high-priority items in the attached matrix. If that aligns, I suggest a short procurement handoff call next Thursday to bring legal and your procurement lead in.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

---

From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@medora.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@medora.ai, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compute handshake: capacity, isolation, and SLA alignment

Thanks, Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we wanted. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Peak behavior: the 400 qps peak is very bursty and lasts for ~20-30 minutes per day (ingest window). Can the burst slots be configured to drain queue without impacting steady-state SLA?
2) Isolation: we will need a written guarantee that PHI workloads will never run on shared GPU partitions; is pool-level isolation sufficient or do you do hypervisor-level separation?
3) Procurement: contracts@medora.ai will need an initial redline within 48 hours to keep our internal approvers moving.

If you can send the SLA draft and the ops matrix we can route it to our security and procurement teams immediately.

Also: we’d like a short canary plan for the first two weeks after cutover — small percentage traffic, validation prompts, and rollback criteria. Can Redwood propose a 5-step canary playbook?

Sofia
Head of ML Ops
Medora Therapeutics
sofia@medora.ai

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Compute handshake: capacity, isolation, and SLA alignment

Karthik — flagged a few commercial items for pricing review. Quick notes: 
- Price anchor: for 12-month reserved pool (6 units + 2 burst), we probably need to propose two tiers: Standard SLA (99.5%) and Premium SLA (99.9% + uptime credit).
- Isolation premium: add a separate line-item for dedicated-node tenancy and KMS integration.
- Implementation estimate: 3-4 weeks for onboarding (ops runbook + security questionnaire closed).

I’ll draft the numbers and put them in the ops matrix, but leave the SLA wording to you since legal will want to review the exact credit language.

Jonas
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@medora.ai>, contracts@medora.ai
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Compute handshake: capacity, isolation, and SLA alignment

Sofia / contracts team — sending the SLA draft and the ops matrix (attached). Highlights and quick responses to your questions below.

- Burst behavior: burst slots are configured as protected burst capacity. They absorb spikes and are designed to drain with priority queueing so steady-state pools maintain p95 latency. We also include pre-warming hooks in the onboarding runbook to reduce KV cold-starts.
- Isolation guarantee: pool-level isolation (dedicated GPU pools) is our standard for PHI workloads; we can add a contractual clause that no multi-tenant GPU slices will host your workloads. For hypervisor-level separation, we can include an architecture note and an R&D checklist, but that will add implementation complexity — happy to discuss specifics on the next call.
- Canary playbook: attached is a 5-step canary outline (traffic carve, functional validation, latency guardrails, model fidelity checks, rollback). We will bind the rollout to objective criteria in the runbook.

Immediate asks from Redwood so we can finalize the commercial proposal:
1) Confirm target go-live month (you mentioned July; we need a signed order before Jun 21 to meet that).
2) Provide the primary procurement contact for redlines (we will send DocuSign + redline link).
3) Any additional regulatory evidence needed beyond SOC2 and monthly audit exports?

Attachments: SLA-draft-Redwood-Medora-20270607.pdf; capacity-proposal-ops-matrix.xlsx

Next: if procurement wants, we’ll stand up a 30-minute redline review with our legal lead tomorrow (Tue) at 9am PT. If that works, I’ll send an invite.

Thanks — Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
